summary.one_liner: VibeVoice is Microsoft's open-source family of voice AI models, covering long-form speech recognition (ASR), multi-speaker text-to-speech (TTS), and real-time streaming TTS.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a family of models built on continuous speech tokenizers running at 7.5 Hz, with an LLM plus diffusion head for generation. VibeVoice-ASR transcribes up to 60 minutes of audio in one pass, producing speaker, timestamp, and content output, and supports customized hotwords. A streaming ASR variant emits text per audio chunk while recording continues, and the README mentions vLLM serving and a finetuning code release. The TTS line includes a long-form multi-speaker model (up to 90 minutes, up to 4 speakers) and VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B, which accepts streaming text input and cites about 300 ms first audible latency. Model weights are linked on Hugging Face, with a BitNet variant aimed at CPU inference. The README also notes Hugging Face Transformers integration and an Azure AI Foundry listing.
use_cases: transcribe long meeting recordings with speaker labels
speech-to-text with custom hotwords for domain terms
live transcription while audio is still arriving
running speech recognition on CPU at the edge
how_to_run: See the documentation links for each model (ASR, TTS, Realtime) for setup
Use the Hugging Face model links to load weights via Transformers
Try the Playground or Colab demos without local setup
notable: Unified ASR producing who, when, and what output in one pass over 60-minute audio
Continuous acoustic and semantic speech tokenizers at 7.5 Hz
Streaming ASR and real-time TTS variants
BitNet quantized ASR model compressed to 1.58 GB for CPU inference
Integrated into Hugging Face Transformers and Azure AI Foundry Labs
caveats: README states the models are intended for research and development only and not recommended for commercial or real-world use without further testing
The TTS code was removed from the repository in September 2025 after misuse, per the README news notes
Outputs may be biased or inaccurate, and the README warns about deepfake and disinformation risks
